name: “Ton Son Nuht” (Larry’s own spelling)
alternateNames: Ton Suhn Nhut / Tah Suhn Nhut (his son's transcriptions, 2026-09-03 and 2026-09-05)
summary: The location Larry remembers as his Company Headquarters — the place he radioed from Núi Bà Đen on the day of the "450 civilians" accusation, and where a medic diagnosed his jaundice days before the medevac. In his own written comments (2026-08-13) Larry spells it "Ton Son Nuht"; the earlier spelling "Thom Son Nuht" was his son's transcription of the name as Larry says it aloud. The leading research hypothesis is Tân Sơn Nhứt (Tan Son Nhut), the major air base adjacent to Saigon; Larry's own spelling is an even closer phonetic match, but the identification still awaits unit records.
researchNotes: Provenance upgraded 2026-08-13: the name is now attested in Larry's own writing ("Ton Son Nuht", twice, in his giscus comments), replacing the earlier secondhand transcription "Thom Son Nuht." His spelling is a very close phonetic match for Tân Sơn Nhứt / Tan Son Nhut, which hosted extensive U.S. Army aviation activity in 1964-1965 — but the identification remains a hypothesis until unit records place his company headquarters there. Note from the unit research (research/units/callsigns-and-units.md): the 118th Aviation Company was based at Bien Hoa, so if his HQ was truly at Tân Sơn Nhứt, a Saigon-based unit (145th Avn Bn HQ elements, or the UTT/68th at Tan Son Nhut) deserves equal weight. No coordinates are recorded until the identification is settled. 2026-08-23 (giscus-stories-c18118912): asked what base his hooch T 123 stood on, Larry answered with the base name again. The form that reached the page, “Thon Sohn Nuht”, is his son’s transcription and not a further rendering from Larry — the comment itself says “I might be misspelling this.” The identification stays plausible on one witness and no documentary support, and no coordinates are set. 2026-09-05: the base gained a layout in his telling, all of it transcribed from the photographs. The EM Club of the floor-show frames (VN-0030 to VN-0034) was 'about 50 yards from my hooch'; the barracks with his bed and mosquito net is where the gibbon Sarge was photographed (VN-0152); the housekeeper of VN-0151 is placed here; a road to the airport end of the base (VN-0067) is the one 'we had to walk down to get a Taxi,' with 'a machine gun nest at the end of the road,' and an orphanage stood 'at the end of the road… somewhat near the machine gun nest' (VN-0070); the road into Saigon ran past a river where children swam (VN-0064); and the 2½-ton truck he drove for the unit may be the one in VN-0080. Each is his placement of a single frame and is rated as such on the photograph. He also puts the AR-15 of VN-0019 here as 'one of the first ones in Vietnam,' which fits the 1964 issue of the rifle to Army aviation and advisory units before the M16 became general.
